transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-03 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~54m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood Partnerships); Raj Patel (Summit Head of Partnerships), Emily Nguyen (Summit Sales Ops), Carlos Mendes (Summit SA), Tara Lee (Summit AE)

Summary:
- Regular partner co-sell / pipeline review; focus on three joint opportunities (RetailEdge, FinServOne, GovData).
- Alignment on lead registration, attribution, joint GTM events, and next technical steps for RetailEdge POC.
- Redwood to provide updated co-sell deck, pricing matrix, and benchmark notes; Summit to provide infra/security details and identify exec sponsor for FinServOne.

Topics discussed:
- Pipeline review by account (RetailEdge - highest priority, FinServOne - large but security-sensitive, GovData - longer timeline)
- Co-sell economics and margin sharing / referral credit process
- Technical validation plan: benchmarks for latency and cost, dedicated vs hosted options, data residency concerns for GovData
- Marketing & events: joint webinar timing and co-branded materials
- Next steps and owners

Transcript:
00:00:05 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 50 minutes today, um, just a quick co-sell pipeline review and then dig into the RetailEdge POC next steps. Can everyone hear ok?
00:00:12 Raj Patel: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Maya.
00:00:18 Emily Nguyen: Good to go.
00:00:25 Liam O'Connor: Hey all, Liam from Redwood. I'll cover the technical asks later.
00:00:33 Carlos Mendes: Great. I have a couple infra questions prepared for the POC.
00:00:45 Maya Chen: Awesome. Quick agenda — one, pipeline run-through; two, co-sell mechanics; three, RetailEdge technical plan; four, action items. Start with pipeline — Raj, do you want to walk the list?
00:01:02 Raj Patel: Sure. We have three primary deals we want to push jointly: RetailEdge, FinServOne, and GovData. RetailEdge is ready to move to POC, they've committed budget for proof of concept but they want a clear SLA and latency targets. FinServOne is much bigger but their procurement and security bar is high — SOC2, data residency, etc. GovData is public sector so that'll need on-prem or VPC and longer procurement cycles.
00:01:35 Maya Chen: Great context. RetailEdge — what's their timeline / decision maker?
00:01:41 Tara Lee: RetailEdge's PM wants a two-week POC then decision. Stakeholders are product lead (Marta), infra lead (Omar), and procurement. They want <150ms 95th percentile for inference on their workloads.
00:01:58 Liam O'Connor: <150ms p95 is achievable on hosted for short sequences but we should validate with their prompt distributions; dedicated pools can guarantee it more predictably under load. We'll need sample traces to size the cluster.
00:02:16 Carlos Mendes: For the POC, RetailEdge will provide a sanitized dataset and examples; we will also need to see token lengths, concurrency patterns.
00:02:27 Emily Nguyen: On attribution / compensation — how does Redwood prefer to handle partner credit? We want lead registration so our reps get credit.
00:02:36 Sofia Alvarez: We typically do partner registration in our portal and then handle referral credits or co-sell margin. For deals that convert we can set referral credit and joint logos for GTM. We'll share the partner economics doc.
00:02:52 Raj Patel: Cool. We also want clarity on deal owner for renewal conversations. Summit reps want to stay in the loop.
00:03:00 Maya Chen: Yes, we expect co-ownership on the account plan. We'll ensure joint account plan spreadsheets include renewal handoffs. I'll send a template.
00:03:12 Raj Patel: Perfect.
00:03:20 Maya Chen: Ok, let's go deeper on RetailEdge POC. Liam, take it away.
00:03:26 Liam O'Connor: Sure. So technical goals: validate latency at target traffic, validate output quality vs their baseline model, and run cost estimates for production. Our proposal is a 2-week POC: week one ingest + baseline tests, week two load tests and wrap-up. We recommend two paths: hosted Redwood API for fastest time-to-value or Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) if they need predictable p95 under sustained load. Hosted is faster to start but can be more variable under noisy neighbor scenarios; Dedicated gives isolation and autoscale policies.
00:04:02 Carlos Mendes: For RetailEdge, they'd prefer not to manage infra; hosting is better, but procurement sometimes balks at shared infra for IP-sensitives. They asked about private deployment (VPC) options too.
00:04:17 Liam O'Connor: We can offer Redwood Private (VPC) for the POC if needed; that adds some lead time for network setup but satisfies data residency and isolation. Need to confirm the exact security requirements.
00:04:28 Tara Lee: RetailEdge's procurement will require SOC2 report and clarifications on KMS. Can you share SOC2 and KMS docs?
00:04:34 Maya Chen: Yes, we'll share SOC2 and security pack after this call (link in follow-up).
00:04:40 Raj Patel: Also the question of pricing for POC — if we do a dedicated pool, do you have temporary pricing?
00:04:48 Sofia Alvarez: For co-sell pilots we typically provide partner pricing tiers; we can discount pilot runs and then standardize for production. We'll include that in the deck.
00:04:59 Emily Nguyen: On commercial terms, Summit will need a written partner referral agreement for our finance team to accept credits.
00:05:06 Maya Chen: We'll loop legal and draft a simple partner referral addendum — I'll own that.
00:05:15 Raj Patel: Ok good. Moving on, FinServOne — big upside but long sales cycle. What do we need from Summit to prioritize it?
00:05:23 Tara Lee: FinServOne requires on-prem or dedicated VPC, plus heavy encryption controls and an exec sponsor at the CIO level. They also require proof of retention and audit logs.
00:05:33 Liam O'Connor: For audit logs and retention we can surface our Console logs and retention policies; for on-prem we can discuss Redwood Private or air-gapped options but that is a much larger engagement. Probably won't fit into a short pilot.
00:05:47 Carlos Mendes: We'll need more details on the customer's existing infra — are they Kubernetes, bare metal, cloud? That will drive feasibility.
00:05:55 Raj Patel: Summit will introduce their CIO contact next week if we agree on materials to send.
00:06:02 Maya Chen: Great — we'll prepare a tailored package for FinServOne highlighting compliance and deployment options.
00:06:09 Emily Nguyen: For GovData, timeline is 9-12 months, mostly procurement. We should keep it on the roadmap but low priority.
00:06:18 Maya Chen: Understood. Marketing — any opportunities for joint events?
00:06:22 Sofia Alvarez: We could do a co-branded webinar post-POC for RetailEdge as a case study, target late April. Summit marketing to co-sponsor and provide speakers.
00:06:32 Raj Patel: That works. We'll commit a marketing lead once RetailEdge POC is successful.
00:06:37 Maya Chen: Alright, now quick technical clarifications — Carlos, what infra details will you send?
00:06:44 Carlos Mendes: We'll send VPC peering requirements, current cluster sizes, and sample request traces by Friday. Also their security checklist.
00:06:53 Liam O'Connor: Perfect. For the POC we also need a small set of representative prompts, expected concurrency (peak sessions), and target sequence lengths. If they can provide token histograms that helps sizing.
00:07:06 Tara Lee: We'll gather and share.
00:07:12 Emily Nguyen: A question on lead registration: what prevents overlaps if Summit and Redwood both pursue the same lead?
00:07:19 Sofia Alvarez: Our partner portal registers the lead with timestamp and partner owner. If overlap occurs we have rules — first registered partner has priority; we can make exceptions for joint registered deals. We'll document the process.
00:07:33 Raj Patel: We need clarity on quote ownership too; Summit wants to be on the quote to help close.
00:07:40 Maya Chen: We can do co-signed quotes for accounts where Summit is actively assisting the deal. We'll note that in the account plan.
00:07:49 Tara Lee: Any blockers you see from Redwood side on RetailEdge?
00:07:53 Liam O'Connor: Only blocker is we need sample data to run the latency/cost benchmarks. Also need a decision on hosted vs dedicated for the POC. If they want dedicated, we need to provision reserved capacity — timeline ~1 week provision after contract. Hosted can be immediate.
00:08:09 Raj Patel: Let's plan to start hosted baseline immediately and spin up dedicated only if p95 doesn't meet their targets. That keeps momentum.
00:08:18 Maya Chen: Sounds practical. We'll propose that in the follow-up.
00:08:24 Emily Nguyen: Great. A couple procurement items: Summit legal will need indemnity caps and standard SLA language; will Redwood accept partner-specific amendments?
00:08:36 Maya Chen: We typically accept partner amendments within reason; major deviations will go to legal. For pilots we keep it light.
00:08:44 Raj Patel: Ok. Anything else on pipeline?
00:08:48 Tara Lee: No, that's it.
00:08:51 Maya Chen: Quick recap of owners: Maya will send co-sell deck, pricing matrix, partner referral template, and SOC2/security pack. Liam will prepare benchmark plan and SOW notes. Carlos will share infra traces and security checklist. Summit will confirm RetailEdge POC contact list and provide sample prompts.
00:09:10 Liam O'Connor: I'll also prepare some notes on autoscaling policy suggestions for RetailEdge and expected cost ranges for hosted vs dedicated.
00:09:19 Sofia Alvarez: I'll draft the marketing plan and webinar timeline.
00:09:24 Raj Patel: We'll identify an exec sponsor for FinServOne and share next week.
00:09:30 Maya Chen: Great. Any risks or red flags?
00:09:34 Carlos Mendes: The main risk is RetailEdge's strict latency target; we'd need to validate quickly or their procurement might pause.
00:09:41 Maya Chen: Understood. We'll prioritize the latency benchmark.
00:09:45 Emily Nguyen: Also need clarity on revenue split and referral credits before Summit's finance signs off.
00:09:51 Sofia Alvarez: We'll include a clear reference sheet for partner economics in the follow-up deck.
00:09:58 Maya Chen: Ok final admin — we'll follow up with links: co-sell deck (https://drive.example.com/summit-cosell-deck), partner portal registration link (https://partners.redwood.ai/register), and SOC2/security pack (https://drive.example.com/redwood-security-pack).
00:10:18 Raj Patel: Thanks Maya. When should we expect the updated materials?
00:10:22 Maya Chen: I'll aim to send the deck and pricing by EOD 2026-03-05. Liam's benchmark plan by 2026-03-10. Carlos to share infra details by 2026-03-06.
00:10:33 Tara Lee: Scheduling note — can we set the technical deep-dive for 2026-03-11 or 12?
00:10:38 Liam O'Connor: 11th works for me.
00:10:41 Raj Patel: Works for us.
00:10:44 Maya Chen: Great — I'll send invite after the materials are shared. Thanks everyone.
00:10:50 Meeting end / small wrap-up chatter (unrelated)

Notes on transcription quality: occasional word swaps and punctuation issues as typical with Fireflies exports.

Attachments / referenced links: https://drive.example.com/summit-cosell-deck (deck), https://drive.example.com/redwood-security-pack (SOC2 + security pack), https://partners.redwood.ai/register (partner portal), joint-account-plan-template (link to spreadsheet will be shared)

End of transcript.
